Empirical Research Plan

1. Identification Strategy

Primary approach = short-window event study.  
Rationale:  The research question is “What is the cost to shareholders when a firm is caught?”  Under the semi-strong form of market efficiency, the stock-price reaction that occurs when the wrongdoing first becomes public incorporates the net present value of all expected future cash-flow and discount-rate effects, giving a direct measure of the total cost.  Because the event date is sharp, standard event-study methods deliver clean causal estimates with minimal functional-form assumptions.  

To decompose the total cost:
• Legal penalties and class-action settlements are observed ex-post in dollars.  
• Balance-sheet corrections (asset write-offs, restatements) are also observed.  
• The difference between the abnormal stock-market loss and the discounted value of the first two items is interpreted as the “reputation” component.

Secondary approach = difference-in-differences on real outcomes to validate the reputation channel and to study heterogeneity.  We track operating performance (sales growth, SG&A-to-sales, R&D cuts, bond‐yield spreads, etc.) for up to five years pre/post and compare the treated firm to a propensity-score-matched control firm that was never investigated.  This establishes whether counterparties actually pull back and whether effects are larger for firms that rely heavily on implicit contracts.

2. Treatment and Control

Treatment variable  
Treated = firm i on the first public disclosure that it is under SEC or DOJ investigation for books-and-records or internal-controls violations.  In practice we use the earliest of (i) first AAER that names the firm, (ii) SEC litigation release, (iii) DOJ press release, or (iv) 8-K/press release announcing an internal investigation.

Event date  
t0 = trading day after the earliest public disclosure (defined above).  Abnormal returns cumulated over [t0−1, t0+1] and [t0−5, t0+5].

Control group  
Event study: CRSP value-weighted market index.  
DID panel: for every treated firm choose one (or three) control firms matched on 3-digit SIC, year-end total assets (±30 %), market-to-book (±30 %), and pre-event return.  Controls must have no SEC/DOJ enforcement actions in our window.

3. Key Identifying Assumptions

Event study  
A1 Market efficiency: prices impound information quickly.  Plausible given U.S. large-cap markets.  
A2 No confounding firm-specific news in the three-day window.  We will search Factiva/EDGAR and drop events with earnings, M&A, or CEO turnover announcements in the window.  
A3 Correct model of normal returns (market-model estimated over [−250, −30]).  Standard in finance; we will run market, industry, and Fama-French models as robustness.

DID  
A4 Parallel trends: in absence of enforcement, treated and matched control firms would have evolved similarly.  Plausibility checked via pre-trend plots.  
A5 No spillovers: one firm’s enforcement action does not affect matched controls (likely except for same-industry contagion; we drop controls in same 4-digit SIC when treated share >25 % of industry sales).

4. Threats to Identification and Mitigation

Threat 1: Information leakage before the recorded event date.  
Fix: Search news back 60 trading days for “investigation,” “accounting irregularities,” etc.  If abnormal returns accumulate before t0 we shift the event date and/or exclude the case.

Threat 2: Other simultaneous bad news (earnings miss, product recall).  
Fix: require “clean” windows verified by Factiva; add dummy controls for confounding announcements; run ±1-day window to minimize overlap.

Threat 3: Selection bias in cross-section (firms with weak governance both cheat and have fragile counterparties).  
Fix: incorporate controls for governance, leverage, performance; in DID we add firm and year fixed effects, and run entropy-balanced weights so covariate means align pre-event.

5. R Code Outline

```r
# Load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(fixest)
library(EventStudy)   # devtools::install_github("mhaentsch/EventStudy")
library(MatchIt)

# 1. Data ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Assume CSVs are in working directory
events  <- read_csv("enforcement_actions.csv")   # one row per action
prices  <- read_csv("crsp_daily.csv")            # permno, date, ret
compust <- read_csv("compustat_annual.csv")      # gvkey, fyear, data
penalty <- read_csv("legal_penalties.csv")       # gvkey, action_id, dollars
writeoff<- read_csv("writeoffs.csv")             # gvkey, action_id, dollars

# 2. Event-study abnormal returns ------------------------------------------
# Step 1: create event window
evt_window <- events %>% 
  mutate(event_date = ymd(first_public_disclosure)) %>% 
  select(permno, action_id, event_date)

# Step 2: market-model parameters
mm_params <- estimateMarketModel(prices, evt_window,
                                 estimation.window = c(-250,-30),
                                 event.window = c(-5,5))

# Step 3: cumulative abnormal return (CAR)
car <- mm_params$car %>% 
  filter(window == "(-1,1)") %>%  # ±1-day window
  select(action_id, CAR)

# 3. Decomposition ---------------------------------------------------------
decomp <- car %>% 
  left_join(penalty,  by="action_id") %>% 
  left_join(writeoff, by="action_id") %>% 
  mutate(legal_loss      = -penalty_dollars/market_cap_pre,
         correction_loss = -writeoff_dollars/market_cap_pre,
         reputation_loss = CAR - legal_loss - correction_loss)

# 4. Cross-sectional determinants ------------------------------------------
cs_reg <- feols(reputation_loss ~ implicit_contracts +
                  r_and_d + intangible_assets +
                  leverage + size + industry_fe,
                data = decomp)
summary(cs_reg)

# 5. DID panel on operating performance ------------------------------------
# Build balanced panel 5 years pre/post
panel <- build_panel(events, compust, match_method = "nearest")  # user-defined

did_reg <- feols(sales_growth ~ treat*post + firm + year,
                 cluster = ~firm,
                 data = panel)
summary(did_reg)

# 6. Robustness: FF-4 factor model CARs ------------------------------------
car_ff <- estimateFamaFrench(prices, evt_window,
                             factors = c("MKT","SMB","HML","UMD"))
```

6. Expected Results

Total CAR around the first disclosure will be strongly negative (≈ −15 % of equity value).  Mean legal and class-action payments will explain ~10 % of that loss; balance-sheet write-offs another 25–30 %; the remaining ~60 % will be attributed to reputation.  Firms with high R&D intensity, high purchase commitments, or large off-balance sheet implicit contracts are expected to suffer an additional −5 % CAR relative to otherwise similar firms.

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (Event Study)

C1: Precise event timing identified …. 1  
C2: No confounding announcements in window …. 0.8  
C3: Efficient capital market assumption …. 1  
C4: Correct model for expected returns …. 0.8  
C5: No sample-selection bias (all detected cases included) …. 0.7  
Overall ≈ 4.3 / 5

End of plan.
